topic.angle: Knotted cords as records in the Andes

body.claim: The Inca used knots tied in a decimal positional system to store numbers and other values on quipu cords.
body.why: A quipu usually consists of cotton or camelid fiber cords, and contains categorized information based on dimensions like color, order, and number. Quipus can have anywhere from a few to several thousand cords. In the early years of the Spanish conquest of Peru, Spanish officials often relied on quipus to settle disputes over local tribute payments or goods production.
